title: Liquidity
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define liquidity, explain why a business can fail without it even while profitable, and name the two ratios that measure it.

blocks.heading: What liquidity means
blocks.text: Liquidity is the ability of a business to pay its short-term debts as they fall due, out of the cash and near-cash assets it holds. A bicycle shop in Copenhagen that owes its suppliers this month and holds plenty of cash and receivables can meet the payment; one whose wealth sits in slow-selling frames may not, because stock must first be sold before the money to pay is there. Liquidity is therefore about timing as much as about size: the question is not only what the business is worth, but what it can lay its hands on when each due date arrives.

blocks.heading: Why liquidity matters
blocks.text: Liquidity failure is the fastest route to closure. Condition: a business lacks the cash to pay a debt on its due date. Mechanism: the unpaid supplier withholds further deliveries or demands payment up front; workers whose wages arrive late lose trust and may leave; the lender may treat the missed payment as a default. Consequence: the business loses the goods, people and credit it runs on, and may be forced to sell assets cheaply or close - even while it is profitable on paper, because profit and cash-flow are not the same thing and the timing of receipts decides what can be paid.

blocks.heading: Measuring liquidity
blocks.text: Liquidity is usually judged with two ratios drawn from the statement of financial position. The current ratio compares all current assets with current liabilities; the acid test removes inventory, the slowest asset to turn into cash. An acid test result below 1 suggests the business is counting on selling stock to pay near-term debts, so a firm with slow-moving stock may need to delay purchases, negotiate longer credit or arrange an overdraft before the due dates arrive. Sub-topic 5.5.3 works both ratios through with figures.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Sub-topic 5.5.3 calculates the two liquidity ratios step by step.
